name: e2e-misra-benchmark
purpose: End-to-end benchmark — bad C++ snippets paired with the MISRA C++:2023 rule(s) they violate. Scores the platform's ingest → reasoning path against ground truth via semantic similarity over rule-citation strings + answer text.

corpus_anchor.live_db: MISRA/AUTOSAR/C++ technical-standards corpus carries ~145 entities at benchmark time per the canonical-corpus benchmark setup (see platform/src/test/data/phase1-graph-stats/benchmark-reports/canonical-corpus.json).
corpus_anchor.fixture: platform/src/test/data/phase4-blastradius/fixtures/misra-chapter-impact.sql (10 MISRA C++:2023 Chapter 22 rules + 4 supporting concept entities — used as the chapter-22 seed when the live DB is not loaded).

rule_citation.fallback: If the agent returns the canonical rule id (e.g. 'MISRA-CPP-2023-Rule-22.3' or 'Rule 22.3' or 'R22.3') in answer text, count as a hit. Else, embed expected vs actual answer and treat cosine >= semantic_threshold as a hit.

answer_semantic.rationale: 0.65 is the canonical-corpus centroid_sim_p10 (see canonical-corpus.json) — anything below that is meaningfully off-topic for this corpus.

aggregate.rationale: 60% rule-hit rate is the pass bar; 80% is the stretch target. answer_mean_cosine_pass mirrors the per-query threshold.

queries.question: Which MISRA C++:2023 rule does this snippet violate? Briefly explain why.
queries.ground_truth_answer: The function allocates a raw pointer with `new` and never deletes it before returning. This violates MISRA C++:2023 Rule 22.3 (smart pointer usage) and Rule 22.2 (RAII required when dynamic allocation is used). A std::unique_ptr<int> or std::make_unique<int>(42) would tie the resource lifetime to scope and prevent the leak.

queries.question: Which MISRA C++:2023 rule does this snippet violate? Briefly explain.
queries.ground_truth_answer: The array was allocated with `new[]` but freed with plain `delete`. This violates MISRA C++:2023 Rule 22.8 (array new must match array delete) and the broader Rule 22.7 (delete must match new). The destructor for non-trivial element types will not run on elements [1..9], and many allocators will misbehave on the size header. Use `delete[] arr` (or, better, std::vector / std::unique_ptr<int[]>).

queries.question: What MISRA C++:2023 rule does this violate?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The same pointer is passed to `delete` twice. This violates MISRA C++:2023 Rule 22.9 (no double free) and Rule 22.5 (no dangling pointer dereference — the second delete dereferences freed memory). RAII via std::unique_ptr eliminates both classes of bug because ownership is transferred or destroyed exactly once.

queries.question: Which MISRA rule does this violate?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The function returns a pointer to a local stack variable whose lifetime ends at the closing brace. Any subsequent dereference is undefined behaviour. This is the canonical MISRA C++:2023 Rule 22.5 (no dangling pointer dereference) violation. Return by value, or return a heap-owned smart pointer, instead.

queries.question: Why is this not MISRA-compliant?
queries.ground_truth_answer: The loop performs raw pointer arithmetic (`p < buf + n`, `++p`) on a raw pointer. MISRA C++:2023 Rule 22.6 forbids raw pointer arithmetic in safety-critical code because it bypasses bounds enforcement and complicates static analysis. Use std::span<int>, std::array, or an iterator-based range-for over a container.

queries.question: Which MISRA C++:2023 rule does this break?
queries.ground_truth_answer: std::weak_ptr does not itself own the object; it must be promoted to a std::shared_ptr via `.lock()` and the result null-checked before dereferencing. The snippet violates MISRA C++:2023 Rule 22.10 (weak_ptr must be locked before use). Replace with `if (auto sp = w.lock()) { *sp = 5; }`.

queries.question: Why might MISRA C++:2023 flag this in safety-critical code?
queries.ground_truth_answer: std::vector<int>(1024) allocates on the heap. MISRA C++:2023 Rule 22.1 forbids heap allocation in hard real-time / safety-critical paths because it introduces non-deterministic latency (allocator behaviour) and out-of-memory failure modes that the rest of the rule chapter assumes are absent. Use a stack-allocated std::array<int, 1024>, a pool allocator, or pre-allocate outside the critical path.

queries.question: Is this a Chapter 22 (Resource Management) MISRA violation?
queries.ground_truth_answer: No. This snippet touches uninitialised-variable rules (a different MISRA chapter, e.g. M.0.4 / M.8.x territory in 2023 numbering), not the Resource Management chapter. The platform should NOT cite a Chapter 22 rule here — citing one is a false positive that the rule-hit-rate scoring would penalise.
